findings.reason: the detection rule must be widened (or the done-when's counts corrected) before §9 is implementable, since as written its own acceptance assertions cannot hold.
findings.text: §9's done-when requires the inventory to report the promoted primitive in `_store.py` and, at the base revision, all four `serve.py` sites, but the stated source-binding rule ("a name bound in the same function body from `with_name`, `with_suffix`, a `/` join on a `.parent`, `NamedTemporaryFile`, `mkstemp` or `mkdtemp`") does not match two binding forms the plan itself must detect: the primitive's own `temporary` is bound from the helper `_open_sibling_temporary` (a tuple assignment, not one of the listed constructors), and `serve.py:503`/`serve.py:567` bind `temporary = Path(handle.name)` from a `NamedTemporaryFile` handle, which the rule reaches only through neither a `str()` wrapper nor a `/`-join — so the owner primitive would read as compliant and the two publishers would not be reported, falsifying both the head assertion ("exactly three functions") and the base inventory requirement.

findings.reason: the plan claims one owner while creating a second executable copy; it should either name which owner is authoritative and how the pin re-run stays in step, or correct the "frozen" justification that licenses the copy.
findings.text: §9 lifts the staged-write predicate out of the census's `primitive_concepts` and lands it as a new function on `reckon/interface_counts.py`, justified because the census is "the frozen code-depth census under docs/research", but that census is a live instrument: §2's done-when appends a pin to `snapshots.json` and re-runs `census.py` at the new head, so after §9 there are two executable owners of the same detection rule (`census.primitive_concepts` and the new `interface_counts` function) with no stated reconciliation.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §8's `write_atomically` is a genuinely deep primitive (it hides temporary creation, rename, fsync, exact mode and directory flush behind one call) and §9 adds no per-caller wrapper, but §9's inventory rule as written is too shallow to name the owner primitive it is built around.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §9 re-implements the census's staged-write predicate as a new owner in `reckon/interface_counts.py` on the ground that the census is "frozen", while §2 of the same plan re-runs `census.py` at each new pin.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — supplied counts public_definitions 1474, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23. §8 and §9 each add exactly one public definition (`write_atomically`; the ported inventory rule) and each states that the retired forks are underscore-private and uncounted, so the public_definitions family cannot shrink — the "state why nothing can be" branch of the rule.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §8 names the owner it extends (`_store._write_through_sibling_temporary`) and §9 names the three mechanisms it reuses or rules out (the census `primitive_concepts` predicate in `docs/research/data/crew-pattern-review/code-depth/census.py`, `interface_counts.read_trees`/`definitions`, and `clones.functions_in`), and I confirmed each exists and holds what the plan says.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one retained layer, `write_json_atomically`, is kept as "the one place a document is serialised, and is not a second owner", a stated reason, satisfying the item; §9 adds no new function to any migrating module.
